Draft reports on semiconductors and skilled workers, the “Surat Model” proposal to help SMEs, transparency in public procurement, and the problem of nominee owners in industry
se: The meeting considered the progress of 3 subcommittees and 1 working group. The Subcommittee on Industry revised 2 draft study reports: raising the semiconductor industry (adding analysis of Thailand's place in the supply chain, investment incentives offered by competing countries, and a proposed fund and strategic mechanism) and developing the workforce for the semiconductor industry (linking skills training with real work, shared laboratories, spreading training centres, and keeping experienced staff). The Subcommittee on Urgent Help for SMEs presented a draft report using Surat Thani Province as a case study. It found 4 main problems: debt and cash flow, not being ready to formalise and grow, competitive disadvantage, and government support that is not joined up. It proposed 5 areas of action, including a local pilot called the “Surat Model”. The meeting suggested adding a “big brother helps little brother” scheme in which stronger businesses support local SMEs, starting in Surat Thani before expanding. The Subcommittee on Promoting SMEs reported information from a representative of a private anti-corruption organisation on risks in public procurement, with proposals such as disclosing beneficial owners, keeping a register of subcontractors and promoting the e-Shopping system, and will hold a forum, “SME Connect: Unlocking Thai SMEs, Linking the Government Market to Business Opportunities”, on 8 December 2026 at Parliament House. The working group on industrial waste management reported progress in pushing for solutions to the use of nominees and grey capital in industry, and the agencies concerned have stepped up inspections and law enforcement.
it: Subcommittee on Industry: revised 2 draft study reports (raising the semiconductor industry, and developing the workforce for the semiconductor industry)
Subcommittee on Urgent Help for SMEs: draft report with Surat Thani as a case study, 5 areas of proposals, the “Surat Model” and the “big brother helps little brother” scheme
Subcommittee on Promoting SMEs: transparency in public procurement, and the “SME Connect” forum (8 December 2026)
Working group on industrial waste management: progress on solving the problem of nominees and grey capital in industry

te: Pre-meeting video · Draft reports on semiconductors and skilled workers, the “Surat Model” proposal to help SMEs, transparency in public procurement, and the problem of nominee owners in industry
Semiconductor report, GI products, online platform fees, field visits in the south, and industrial waste
se: The committee considered progress from 3 subcommittees and 1 working group. The Industry subcommittee has finished all 5 chapters of its study report on upgrading the semiconductor industry, plans a study visit to a private semiconductor company in Bangkok (20 Nov 2026) and a seminar to share its findings, “Driving the Electronics Industry of the Future” (27 Nov 2026). The subcommittee on urgent help for SMEs reported on upgrading geographical indication (GI) products, lower fees on online platforms, the rules on trade credit terms, and the “Surat Mahanakhon” idea, and proposed a working group on using artificial intelligence (AI) to support SMEs and communities. The subcommittee on promoting SMEs and special economic zones summarised its study visit to Songkhla and Pattani (6–8 Nov 2026), for example the potential as a trade gateway, costs in industrial estates and the effects of fishing control measures. The working group on industrial waste management reported its observations from visiting 3 factories in Samut Sakhon, which are being checked with the agencies concerned, and the committee will visit Chon Buri to follow up complaints about industrial factories.
it: Industry subcommittee: semiconductor upgrading report completed (5 chapters), private-sector study visit (20 Nov 2026) and the seminar “Driving the Electronics Industry of the Future” (27 Nov 2026)
Subcommittee on urgent help for SMEs: GI products, online platform fees, credit terms, the Surat Mahanakhon idea and a proposed AI working group for SMEs and communities
Subcommittee on promoting SMEs and special economic zones: study visit to Songkhla and Pattani (6–8 Nov 2026)
Working group on industrial waste management: field visit in Samut Sakhon, and a visit to Chon Buri to follow

se: The committee noted the work of 3 subcommittees, such as workforce development for the printed circuit board industry and SMEs in electronic government procurement (e-GP). te: Motion on pollution in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya: hearing the senator who proposed it
se: The committee noted the work of 3 subcommittees, such as electricity and water readiness for semiconductor investment, upgrading small businesses into micro SMEs (private-sector bodies heard) and SMEs' access to letters of guarantee in government procurement. It then considered the motion asking the Senate to consider solutions to pollution in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya, inviting Mr. Chinnachot Saengsang, the senator who proposed it.
it: Work of the 3 subcommittees (industry · urgent help for SMEs · promoting SMEs and special economic zones in government procurement and online markets)
Motion asking the Senate to consider solutions to pollution in Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya (the senator who proposed it invited)

te: Following up the Thai SELECT report, and a complaint on oversight of digital platforms
se: The committee noted the industry subcommittee's work on quality oversight of steel production and the shift from IF furnaces to EF/EA, noted progress after the Senate considered the report on upgrading the Thai SELECT mark, and considered a complaint asking for a check on enforcement of the 2022 Royal Decree on digital platform services that require notification, with the Trade Competition Commission of Thailand (TCCT) invited.
it: Industry subcommittee: quality oversight of steel production and the shift away from IF furnaces
Progress after the Senate considered the report on upgrading the Thai SELECT mark
Complaint asking for a check on enforcement of the law on digital platform services (TCCT invited)

te: Subcommittees report: semiconductor workforce, OTOP in Surat Thani, and SMEs in government procurement
se: At this meeting Mr. Niphon Ekawanit, First Vice-Chairperson, acted as chair. The committee noted the work of 3 subcommittees: developing the workforce for the semiconductor industry, upgrading OTOP producers into micro SMEs (a Surat Thani case study), and obstacles for SMEs in government procurement (the State Audit Office and the Department of Special Investigation heard), such as how terms of reference and past-work criteria are set.
cre: First Vice-Chair of the committee, presiding at the meeting
it: Work of the 3 subcommittees (industry · urgent help for SMEs · promoting SMEs and special economic zones in government procurement and online markets)
